messages:
OpsBot: :rotating_light: ALERT: KV-cache error rate spike on shard-pool eu-west-1-gpu-42. 5xx rate from embed/serve increased to 18% over 5m. Paging increased by 4x. Incident created: INC-2080001234
Maya: seeing it, thanks. noisy host list: node-42, node-43 showing large inflight KV cache evictions.
Tom: any NCCL errors in the logs?
Li: pulling logs now. early glance shows repeated NCCL_TIMEOUT and tensor-partition mismatch warnings around 2080001280.
Dena: customer-facing impact? which tenants?
Maya: dedicated clusters for two mid-market customers (cust-alpha, cust-beta) seeing timeouts and slow responses; hosted traffic experiencing latency cliff (p95 from 120ms -> 1.2s).
Santiago: sounds like the recent continuous-batching tweak + new KV sharding code might be interacting badly. I pushed the sharding change in last deploy 2080000200.
oncall-Tilly: I'm oncall, stepping in. Tilly here. Assigning incident lead to ops (Maya). Taking notes.
Maya: plan: 1) throttle continuous-batching globally to baseline, 2) disable KV-auto-shard fallback so we avoid uneven partitioning, 3) if NCCL persists, revert sharding roll.
Tom: agree. hotfix commands below to lower continuous batching threshold and flush cache prefix for affected pool:
```
# reduce continuous batch size
redwoodctl config set runtime.continuous_batch.max_tokens=64 --scope=eu-west-1
# flush KV prefix for pool
redwoodctl kv flush --pool shard-pool --prefix eu-west-1-gpu-42
```
Li: running the config change now (reducing max_tokens). Patch applied at 2080001292.
OpsBot: Deploy bot: config-change applied by Li (runtime.continuous_batch.max_tokens -> 64) at 2080001292.
Dena: started cache prefix flush on node-42 and node-43 (async). progress: node-42 20% node-43 15%.
Santiago: I'm watching NCCL metrics — inter-GPU transfers dropped after throttle, but we still see partition hotness on shard 7 (holds 45% of tokens). that skew explains the hot evictions.
Maya: can we force rebalancer to rebalance all KV partitions? risk: extra traffic but should reduce hot spots.
Tom: there's an immediate safe mode: enable replica-read routing for shard 7 -> route reads to replica until rebalance completes. Command:
```
redwoodctl kv set-routing --shard 7 --prefer replica
```
Applying that now.
Li: routing change applied at 2080001310. latency for affected requests p95 dropping from 1.2s -> 420ms for a subset of traffic.
Dena: cache eviction rate falling, but paging still elevated because pages are being refilled while rebalancer runs.
Santiago: starting rebalance run with debug logging. initiating at 2080001320. ETA ~3m.
OpsBot: Rebalancer started by Santiago at 2080001320.
Maya: customer impact update: cust-alpha performance restored to acceptable levels, cust-beta still has intermittent 5xx for heavy multimodal calls (likely pinned large KV pages). Support notified and postmortem ticket created.
oncall-Tilly: handing off to eng-ml (Santiago) for overnight mitigation and root cause — I'm available for escalation.
Santiago: will continue. immediate next steps: collect shard mapping snapshot, compare pre/post deploy mapping, and examine the sharding hash function edge-case for short sequences.
Tom: also capturing NCCL stack traces and kernel logs for the period 2080001260-2080001320. attaching in incident doc.
Maya: summary for incident bridge: cause = interaction of continuous-batching config + recent KV sharding change produced uneven partitioning -> hotspot -> paging surge -> NCCL timeouts due to tensor-parallel imbalance. mitigation = throttle continuous batching, prefer replica reads for hot shard, flush prefixes, trigger rebalance; follow-up = revert sharding change if root repro, add guards in rebalancer to avoid >x% skew, add autosafe to continuous-batching config.
Dena: customer comms draft: short note + apology + mitigation steps + ETA for postmortem. sending to legal for review.
OpsBot: Incident status: mitigated->partial (errors reduced, some intermittent 5xx remain). next update in 30m or on-hand-off.
Santiago: capturing state dumps now and will run a reproducer on a staging tensor-parallel cluster that mirrors the short-seq distribution.
Maya: thanks everyone. leaving thread for the overnight owner handoff. oncall-Tilly stays available.
oncall-Tilly: acknowledged handoff. logging this as handoff to eng-ml @2080001360. Good job — we'll iterate on a postmortem and long-term fixes.
